question: According to the Utah CDL Manual, what is a converter dolly?
choice_a: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig
choice_b: A hydraulic lift used to raise the landing gear of a semitrailer
choice_c: A braking device installed only on the last trailer of a triple combination
choice_d: A locking mechanism that secures the kingpin directly to the tractor frame
explanation: The manual defines a converter dolly as a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.1 (Figure 7.1 caption)

question: How do you release the brakes on a converter dolly that is equipped with spring brakes, before wheeling it into position?
choice_a: Open the air tank petcock
choice_b: Use the dolly parking brake control
choice_c: Pull the tractor's trailer air supply knob
choice_d: Disconnect the emergency line shut-off valve
explanation: The manual instructs releasing dolly brakes by opening the air tank petcock, or, if the dolly has spring brakes, using the dolly parking brake control instead.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Position Converter Dolly in Front of Second (Rear) Trailer

question: Before backing a converter dolly under the rear trailer, how should the trailer height compare to the center of the dolly's fifth wheel?
choice_a: It must be exactly level with the fifth wheel
choice_b: It must be several inches higher than the fifth wheel
choice_c: It must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly as the dolly is pushed under
choice_d: Trailer height does not matter as long as the kingpin is aligned
explanation: The manual states the trailer height must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: After backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer, how do you test that the coupling has taken hold?
choice_a: Sound the horn and watch whether the trailer shifts
choice_b: Check the air pressure gauge in the cab
choice_c: Have a helper stand on the trailer's landing gear
choice_d: Pull against the pin of the second semitrailer
explanation: The manual directs the driver to test the coupling by pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer before making a visual check.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: When making a visual check of a completed dolly-to-trailer coupling, what should you look for?
choice_a: No visible space between the upper and lower fifth wheel, with the locking jaws closed on the kingpin
choice_b: That the landing gear crank handle has been removed
choice_c: That the safety chains are shiny and free of rust
choice_d: That the tractor's fuel tank is full
explanation: The manual's visual check specifies no visible space between the upper and lower fifth wheel and locking jaws closed on the kingpin.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: Near the end of the coupling procedure, after raising the landing gear completely, what should you do to confirm the brake system is working?
choice_a: Disconnect the electrical cord to test the running lights
choice_b: Charge trailer brakes by pushing the "air supply" knob in, then check for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off
choice_c: Release the pintle hook to confirm it is unlocked
choice_d: Lower the landing gear again to test its strength
explanation: The manual instructs charging trailer brakes (pushing the air supply knob in) and checking for air at the rear of the second trailer via the emergency line shut-off, noting that if air pressure isn't there something is wrong and the brakes won't work.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: When uncoupling the rear trailer of a set of twin trailers, when does the manual say to chock the wheels of the second trailer?
choice_a: Always, regardless of brake type
choice_b: Only if parked on a hill
choice_c: If it doesn't have spring brakes
choice_d: Chocking is never required for this procedure
explanation: The uncoupling procedure directs the driver to chock the wheels of the second trailer if it doesn't have spring brakes.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers - Uncouple Rear Trailer

question: Why does the procedure call for lowering the landing gear of the second semitrailer slightly before pulling the converter dolly out?
choice_a: To level the trailer for weighing
choice_b: To disconnect the electrical cord automatically
choice_c: To engage the trailer's parking brake
choice_d: To remove some weight from the dolly
explanation: The manual states to lower the landing gear of the second semitrailer enough to remove some weight from the dolly before pulling it out.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers - Uncouple Rear Trailer

question: Why does the manual warn against unlocking the pintle hook while the converter dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it very difficult to re-couple
choice_b: It automatically triggers the emergency brakes on all trailers
choice_c: It voids the manufacturer's warranty on the dolly
choice_d: It causes the air tank petcock to jam shut
explanation: The manual specifically warns that the dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it very difficult to re-couple, if the pintle hook is unlocked while the dolly is still under the trailer.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncouple Converter Dolly

question: Which of these is a correct step when uncoupling the converter dolly from the first semitrailer?
choice_a: Raise the dolly landing gear before disconnecting the safety chains
choice_b: Apply the converter gear spring brakes or chock the wheels, then release the pintle hook on the first semi-trailer
choice_c: Disconnect the fifth wheel latch before lowering the landing gear
choice_d: Leave the safety chains connected until the tractor is parked
explanation: The manual's sequence for uncoupling the converter dolly includes applying converter gear spring brakes or chocking wheels, then releasing the pintle hook on the first semi-trailer before slowly pulling clear.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncouple Converter Dolly

question: What is the correct method described for adding the third trailer when assembling a triple-trailer combination?
choice_a: Couple all three trailers to the tractor simultaneously at a single connection point
choice_b: Couple the second and third trailers together before attaching either one to the tractor
choice_c: Couple the tractor to the first trailer, then move the converter dolly into position and couple the first trailer to the second trailer using the method for coupling doubles
choice_d: Use a specialized triple-only coupling device not used for doubles
explanation: The manual says to couple the tractor to the first trailer using the tractor-semitrailer method, then move the converter dolly into position and couple the first trailer to the second trailer using the method already described for coupling doubles, completing the triples rig.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.3 Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: What is the first step described for uncoupling a triple-trailer rig?
choice_a: Uncouple the tractor from the first trailer
choice_b: Release all pintle hooks on the rig at the same time
choice_c: Disconnect the first trailer's landing gear
choice_d: Uncouple the third trailer by pulling the dolly out, then unhitch the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles
explanation: The manual states to first uncouple the third trailer by pulling the dolly out, then unhitch the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles, before uncoupling the remainder of the rig as a standard double-bottom rig.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.3 Uncouple Triple-trailer Rig

question: What does the manual say a driver should do about coupling and uncoupling truck-trailer or tractor-trailer combinations not specifically described in the manual?
choice_a: Learn the correct way to couple and uncouple that vehicle according to the manufacturer and/or owner specifications
choice_b: Assume it couples the same way as a standard set of doubles
choice_c: Contact the DMV for a special waiver before driving it
choice_d: Only ever drive combinations explicitly listed in the manual
explanation: The manual notes there are too many combination types to cover and instructs drivers to learn the correct coupling/uncoupling method according to the manufacturer and/or owner specifications.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.4 Coupling and Uncoupling Other Combinations

question: What inspection procedure does the manual direct you to use as the basis for inspecting a doubles or triples combination vehicle?
choice_a: A simplified three-step check unique to combination vehicles
choice_b: The seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2
choice_c: A manufacturer-specific checklist only, without reference to Section 2
choice_d: The pre-trip air brake test from Section 5 alone
explanation: The manual says to use the seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2 to inspect the combination vehicle, then adds items specific to combinations.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3 Inspecting Doubles and Triples

question: When inspecting the lower fifth wheel on a doubles or triples combination, where should the locking jaws be positioned on the kingpin?
choice_a: Around the head of the kingpin, not the shank
choice_b: Anywhere on the kingpin, since exact position doesn't matter
choice_c: Around the shank of the kingpin, not the head
choice_d: Behind the release arm, away from the kingpin entirely
explanation: The additional coupling-system checks specify that the locking jaws should be around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks - Coupling System Areas

question: What should you check on the upper fifth wheel (mounted on the trailer) during a doubles/triples inspection?
choice_a: That the crank handle has been removed
choice_b: That the spare tire is secured
choice_c: That the emergency line shut-off is closed
choice_d: That the glide plate is securely mounted to the trailer frame and the kingpin is not damaged
explanation: The manual's upper fifth wheel check specifies the glide plate must be securely mounted to the trailer frame and the kingpin must not be damaged.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks - Coupling System Areas

question: Why should you check that the sliding fifth wheel is not positioned too far forward on the combination?
choice_a: So the tractor frame won't hit the landing gear, or the cab won't hit the trailer, during turns
choice_b: So the trailer's emergency brakes will release properly
choice_c: So the converter dolly will be easier to attach
choice_d: So the safety chains will have less slack
explanation: The manual warns to check that the fifth wheel is not so far forward that the tractor frame will hit the landing gear, or the cab will hit the trailer, during turns.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks - Sliding Fifth Wheel

question: What should you verify about the landing gear during a doubles/triples pre-trip inspection?
choice_a: That it is lowered halfway to allow quick access
choice_b: That it is fully raised, has no missing parts, is not bent or damaged, and the crank handle is in place and secured
choice_c: That it is painted to match the trailer color
choice_d: That it has recently been lubricated with brake fluid
explanation: The manual's landing gear check requires it to be fully raised, with no missing parts, not bent or otherwise damaged, and the crank handle in place and secured.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks - Landing Gear

question: On a set of double or triple trailers, what position should the shut-off valves be in at the rear of the front trailer(s) versus the rear of the last trailer?
choice_a: Both should be closed
choice_b: Both should be open
choice_c: Rear of the front trailer(s) should be OPEN; rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED
choice_d: Rear of the front trailer(s) should be CLOSED; rear of the last trailer should be OPEN
explanation: The manual states that shut-off valves at the rear of front trailers should be OPEN, while the rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks - Double and Triple Trailers

question: What position should the converter dolly's air tank drain valve be in during inspection?
choice_a: Open
choice_b: Half-open, to allow condensation to drain continuously
choice_c: Removed entirely before driving
choice_d: Closed
explanation: The manual lists the converter dolly air tank drain valve as an item that must be CLOSED.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks - Double and Triple Trailers

question: During the "Check That Air Flows to All Trailers" test, what does hearing air escaping when you open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer indicate?
choice_a: The entire air system is charged
choice_b: There is a dangerous air leak that must be repaired immediately
choice_c: The tractor protection valve has failed
choice_d: The trailer brakes are not connected
explanation: The manual states that hearing air escaping at the rear emergency line shows the entire system is charged; if you do NOT hear air escaping, you should check that the shut-off valves are open.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks - Check That Air Flows to All Trailers

question: During the tractor protection valve test, within what pressure range does the manual say the trailer air supply control usually pops out to the emergency position?
choice_a: 5 to 10 psi
choice_b: 20 to 45 psi
choice_c: 60 to 90 psi
choice_d: 100 to 120 psi
explanation: The manual states the trailer air supply control should pop out (go from normal to emergency) when air pressure falls into the range specified by the manufacturer, usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks - Test Tractor Protection Valve

question: How does the manual describe testing the trailer emergency brakes on a doubles or triples combination?
choice_a: Apply the foot brake pedal firmly while the vehicle is parked
choice_b: Disconnect the electrical cord and observe whether the trailer rolls
choice_c: Charge the trailer air brake system, check that the trailer rolls freely, then pull out the trailer air supply control (or place it in "emergency" position) and pull gently on the trailer with the tractor to check that the emergency brakes are on
choice_d: Open the service line shut-off valve fully and listen for a hiss
explanation: The manual describes charging the trailer air brake system, confirming the trailer rolls freely, then pulling out the trailer air supply control or placing it in the emergency position and pulling gently with the tractor to confirm the emergency brakes engage.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks - Test Trailer Emergency Brakes

question: According to the manual, how should trailer service brakes be tested, versus how they are controlled during normal operation?
choice_a: Tested and controlled only with the hand valve (trolley valve)
choice_b: Tested with the foot pedal, but controlled in normal operation with the hand valve
choice_c: Tested and controlled only with the foot pedal; the hand valve is for parking only
choice_d: Tested with the hand control (trolley valve), but controlled in normal operation with the foot pedal
explanation: The manual notes the trailer brakes should be tested with the hand valve, but are controlled in normal operation with the foot pedal, which applies air to the service brakes at all wheels.
source_note: Utah CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks - Test Trailer Service Brakes
